title: Measurement: an interactive session on Windows and Node 24 quit within 50 ms of Pi ending a second turn that completed a tool call exits cleanly through the supervisor
summary: ACC-0088's interactive observation under the condition the Node 24 abort needed: a real interactive Kiln session on Windows 11 and Node 24.18.0 at a3ad951 (job mode default, one shared 8,000 ms budget), quit immediately after a completed tool call on a SECOND turn, timed from Pi's own turn end. HOW: start-kiln's own main() and the real supervisor ran in Windows Terminal, wrapped only to retain the returned record and the exit status. A harness-only extension in the manual project's agent directory appended Pi's turn_end, agent_end and agent_settled events with their times. Turn one was text only. Turn two was answered with a kiln_project_status tool call; Pi ran it, sent its result, and the provider answered with text. /quit had been typed during turn two, and Enter was sent a set delay after the harness saw turn two's agent_end. Keys were real input events sent to a window verified to be in the foreground. RESULT: run R4, Enter 9 ms after agent_end; run R5, Enter 44 ms after agent_end (agent_settled fired in the same millisecond as agent_end in both). Each: Pi exited with code 0, not the abort code 3221226505; the process exited 0; the shutdown record says trigger agent-exit, complete, budget.ms 8000 with 515 ms and 466 ms spent, nothing unobserved or unfinished, both trees stopped through their jobs with both hosts exited, the launcher stopped gracefully without escalation, the port free, exactly the run's own run file removed with none failed. An outside process watcher then found nothing of the run alive, the port refused connections, and the temporary directories and the project's runtime directory were unchanged. Pi's transcript shows the sequence: user, assistant stop; user, assistant toolUse kiln_project_status, toolResult, assistant stop.
